newsitem.title: USA: US CREDIT OUTLOOK - Eye on oil prices pre-payrolls.
newsitem.headline: US CREDIT OUTLOOK - Eye on oil prices pre-payrolls.

text.p: A sparse economic calendar will keep U.S. credit market participants firmly focused on oil market uncertainty on Wednesday, even as they begin positioning themselves for Friday's nervously anticipated payrolls report.
Oil prices rose sharply on Tuesday, then retreated from the day's highs, after market players returned from a long Labor Day weekend to news of U.S. military action against Iraq.

The attack came in response to Baghdad's incursion into protected Kurdish zones in northern Iraq, which led to the suspension of a deal allowing Iraq to sell up to $2.0 billion in oil for food and medicine over the next six months.
Economists said the oil price gains could have a marginally negative impact on the inflation outlook if they persist. As a result, they could keep the market occupied ahead of the employment release.

"I'm sure the market will watch the oil price developments and we'll probably also see some position squaring ahead of payrolls," said Joseph Carson, chief fixed income economist at Deutsche Morgan Grenfell.

Analysts expect the payrolls report to shed more definitive light on the strength of third quarter economic growth as well as the prospects for a Federal Reserve interest-rate tightening at its upcoming September 24 meeting.
The Fed has refrained from hiking rates in recent months in the hope that growth would taper off in the second half of the year.
"I think people are still trying to gauge whether the Fed is doing enough, soon enough," said Russell Sheldon, senior economist at Mellon Bank Corp.
Wednesday's data schedule consists of BTM/Schroders weekly retail sales data, due at 0900 EDT/1300 GMT, and July construction spending figures, due from the Commerce Department at 1000 EDT/1400 GMT.
Analysts played down the importance of the weekly sales data given the Tuesday release of the more closely-watched Redbook retail sales report.

Economists polled by Reuters expect construction spending to dip by 0.2 percent in the July report versus a gain of 1.2 percent in June. They are not expecting this report to have much market impact either.

In late trading on Tuesday, the benchmark 6.75 percent 30-year bond was up 21/32 at 96-03/32 to yield 7.06 percent. The federal funds rate is expected to open between 5-5/16 and 5-7/16 percent on Wednesday.
